notes.title: The Electric Chair and The Joy Drinker Statue
notes.content:
Here's a brand new update about The Eldritch Zookeeper's development:
[previewyoutube=6GWo-zw3d-k;full][/previewyoutube]
There's a brand new electricity grid system in The Eldritch Zookeeper:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/50c541cf4cda0362d55908474868d6dbb2e701c1.png[/img]
See those yellow lines? Those are electric power lines running between all the lampposts and all the electric buildables in your zoo.

Where does the power come from? 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/872607d5b237e2772023aab4660a288c715aba9b.png[/img]
All those happy zoo visitors are now a non-polluting power source for your zoo expansion! Congratulations to each and every one of them. Whenever they walk beneath the statue's open hand, their joy is turned into useful charge, and will zip about your electrical grid to wherever it needs to go.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/1e8f31a6237454e464c9ae4a43451b9d4ca079d4.png[/img]
The Electric Chair is the first new powered device that needs a strong electrical input. Recharge your staff automatons in what we [i]really, really hope[/i] is a non-painful way of getting them busy after depleting their battery. There's no reliable evidence that the automatons feel pain and there's [i]certainly[/i] no way they can complain about it if they do, so it's fine.

The automatons can also hold scythes and cut the grass for you! How helpful of them.

Check out that video for more info! More updates on the way, stay tuned...
- Matt

notes.title: Stone Paths, Grass and a Big Scythe
notes.content:
Here's a brand new update about The Eldritch Zookeeper's development:
[previewyoutube=LNAtJuTIFVI;full][/previewyoutube]
Stone paths! At long last. And they look so gooood.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/155670053953daf11520a980405ef425e8d2bff6.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/46b5cbd7bb7d45283f8faba843ffc0394c415266.png[/img]
It's taken a lot of tweaking to get the construction of the stone paths feeling right. You sort of 'paint' the path onto the ground as you run about, and that looks and sounds really satisfying. I'd like to add a few different path variations that you can choose between, and will change the look of your zoo pretty drastically.

Grass that grows is the other Big New Thing, and if you let your zoo get a bit out of control in that regard, it's a bit of a mess:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/3ee9566cd4075ac8940037615bfb86bbc7478c71.png[/img]
So you've got to invest in a scythe - a new item! - and get cutting, or else the visitors are going to start complaining at the state of your zoo. And if you happen to scythe a visitor or two on the way? Well, this is The Eldritch Zoo, not The Safety Zoo, what do you expect?

Check out that video to see all of that in motion! More updates on the way, stay tuned...
- Matt

notes.title: Magical (and Helpful) Automatons
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/3fe55edd303ee352f539e17835bb1ee854989b1b.gif[/img]

[i]Doo doo doo doo[/i] (that's the sound I think it makes to itself as it runs along.)

I've added staff you can hire to help you with your zookeeping, they're these big battery-with-legs-and-arms-and-a-lantern-as-a-head things, and they're pretty helpful:

[previewyoutube=JeJs5hBSzCs;full][/previewyoutube]
The gameplay issue I allude to that video is that maintaining big zoos was increasingly difficult, the larger they got. It wasn't hard to [i]build[/i] a big zoo, it was keeping it going that was challenging. At a certain point there were just too many monsters needing food, too many litter bins needing emptying, just too many jobs for one player to manage. Because, remember, if a monster goes hungry, after a little while they get agitated, then angry, and they start breaking stuff and killing everything they can get their teeth/claws/tentacles into.

But with staff to do all the busywork for you, you can keep expanding and building, and investing in new monsters and redesigning your zoo without having to do a full-zoo circuit to keep everything going. Of course, you have to invest in these staff first and scale up the right way, but the automatons are already really helping.

As I say in the video, there's a few more things I think these automatons can help with, and I'd like to make them upgradable and more efficient. But it's a good start!

Here's a few links so you can keep in touch:

[list]
[*] [url=https://cranktrain.com/guild/]The Guild Of Cursed Zookeepers[/url] - Get a free Zookeeper character for The Eldritch Zookeeper!
[*] [url=http://discord.gg/cranktrain]Our lovely Discord server[/url]
[*] [url=https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCVCz-_8VfkVwgB1WzCcuq4w]Go on, do a subscribe.[/url]
[/list]
More updates coming soon.
Matt

notes.title: Mad Science!
notes.content:
[i]Science.[/i]

Sure, it's been around since the enlightenment, but that was [i]ages[/i] ago. If you're bored of physics, chemistry - and who isn't? Who wants to study rocks and rock-adjacent stuff? - Then perhaps it's time to look to the fringes? [b]Alchemical Black Science![/b] That's the really exciting stuff, and it's even more exciting because it's [i]forbidden[/i].

The bonus is you don't have to worry about all that pesky 'ethics board' nonsense. Watch the update video all about the new research lab:
[previewyoutube=aeDp8B5R6aE;full][/previewyoutube]
Brains floating in a jar do all the work for us, how kind of them.

Adding a tech-tree full of research options has been a long time coming, and now the cackling mad scientist has arrived at last, I can continue to fill it up with all sorts of interesting additions, and 'New Stuff'. My plan is to first make the research tree of options [i]broad[/i] (as in, at the very start of any game you can choose a wide array of ) and then [i]deep[/i] (some research items need to be unlocked before others, and these can be chained together.) Do you 'go deep' on one particularly promising looking vein of research? Or do you instead dabble here and there in the shallow end?

Whatever you research; new monsters, new shops, upgrades and enhancements, they're going to improve your Zoo's Visitor Satisfaction Rating that [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ifq1AFlQHxY]we talked about last time[/url].

One advantage of having a broad tech-tree is that you can start off a zoo in a very different way. There's no 'best build order', or at least, there'll be quite a number of viable options.

[h3]Guild of Cursed Zookeepers May Only Bonus![/h3]
Are you a member of the Guild Of Cursed Zookeepers? That's where you go to https://cranktrain.com/guild/ and link your Steam account to your Discount account for a free character named Kristof:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/96f4d7475ad87a3f0fd24c1750731bfbd45d0566.png[/img]

For the month of May only I'm also giving away 'Izsak's Skullish Mask':

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/c070b4384c9b2cd4f0b21f85f4657907f8b0c743.png[/img]

It's a hat! Like in Team Fortress 2 or one of those games, just a fun bonus, and it exists as a Steam Inventory Item. If you head to the [url=https://cranktrain.com/guild/]guild website[/url] and claim it now, you'll get it when the game comes out.

If it's something people (like you!) enjoy, perhaps we could have a free bonus gift like this every month? Let me know!

Till next time,
Matt

notes.title: Bathrooms and Smoothie Shops!
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29396689/00fdefde166a421c3efc0e7d705794f35531a059.png[/img]

Another game update for you! I've made another video and you can [b]watch it here:[/b]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uAi662Ehc1Q
In summary:

• [b]Smoothie Shops![/b] After having Ice Cream shops in the game, now it's not just food, there's drinks too

• [b]Bathrooms![/b] If there's both food and drink in the game, it makes sense the visitors will need something else, right?

I think a next step of mine is to let the player know exactly how well they are doing with meeting the needs of the zoo guests. Some kind of global Visitor Satisfaction Rating that runs from 0 to 100, and perhaps some way of breaking that down into specific needs as well. How well you're doing with satisfying visitor's desires is going to correlate with how popular your zoo is... which of course leads to how many new visitors are going to turn up, which in turn powers your economic engine that lets you keep expanding and feeding your existing monsters so they don't go absolutely mad and kill everyone. <- This is the Game Loop, as they call it.

That's it for now! [b]Join us[/b] on our Discord for a closer look at development: https://discord.gg/cranktrain

notes.title: Litter Bins, Ticket Booths and Benches for Visitors!
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29396689/c4792279159412949d413d21ef31305590166c00.png[/img]

Another [i]big[/i] ol' game update for you! [b]Watch it here:[/b]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-fvjXmE8rgw
In summary:

• [b]Bins![/b] Litter can become a big problem and lead to dissatisfied or even angry visitors. You'll have to build them at appropriate points all around the zoo, and keep them empty.

• [b]Ticket Booth![/b] A new visitor flow for entering and exiting the zoo, centring around buying tickets for the waistcoated, friendly helper near the entrance. Don't mind the mask, it's got a smile on it! That counts for something, right? Right?

• [b]Benches![/b] The metal bench can seat three visitors, letting them rest and keeping them happy. If they don't have seating, visitors are going to be quicker to leave and go home, but if they're in your zoo they can spend their money! Like bins, they have to be positioned all around the zoo, for easy access.

That's it for now! [b]Join us[/b] on our Discord for a closer look at development: https://discord.gg/cranktrain

notes.title: Introducing the HypnoLlama! (And the HypnoLlama Queen!)
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29396689/0e1bd14626296007b866cea8e608de8e2709bc97.png[/img]

The Eldritch Zookeeper has a new trailer! To announce not one, but two new monsters to begrudgingly welcome to the monster zoo.

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WVuMhw7S1Kw][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29396689/af6bce7c718673d01542c7d304718598306f332d.png[/img][/url]

The HypnoLlama is a friendly-looking thing, indeed of all the monsters it appears, on first glance, to be almost normal. But looks can be deceiving, and that is why I never open my eyes, not ever. Because when the HypnoLlama gets agitated, maybe you've let it go hungry, or you've let it get too close to humans, or another monster is biting it - it has the tendency to grow angry and take over lesser minds. 'Lesser minds', in this case, are your zoo visitors. Hypnotised guests are filled with a thirst for destruction and, left unchecked, can quickly turn a nicely ordered zoo into a chaotic mess.

The HypnoLlama Queen, if you can imagine, is even worse. It... sort of looks like a bunch of HypnoLlama's have melted into each other? Perhaps that's exactly what has happened? On one hand, sure, it doesn't take up much space, and doesn't move around very much. But when angry it is an order of magnitude more dangerous than your everyday, run-of-the-mill HypnoLlama.

You'll also notice from the trailer a new voice! The definitely-evil skeleton who seems quite responsible for the zookeeper's cursed situation is played by actor Scott Gilmour. Some voice acting is a great new addition that I'm really excited about.

Oh! Also! We now have a Discord Server! We're a pleasant, chill group, so if that sounds like where you want to be, and to hear about the game as development continues, you can join us here: https://discord.gg/C6TdkaP

I'm still hard at work making this game, so follow along for more news:

• Twitter: http://twitter.com/MattLuard

- Matt

notes.title: The 'Bigger Zoos' Update!
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29396689/6b7e47f6855d4853209b7393ca0c5214e899a0b7.png[/img]
Hello! I'm Matt, I'm the lead developer and... well, I guess the only developer on The Eldritch Zookeeper. It's time to share an update on how things with the game have been progressing over the last while!

If you're new to The Eldritch Zookeeper, here's what you need to know:
[list]
    [*] It's a game about managing a zoo, but the zoo is full of monsters.
    [*] The game's not quite ready for release yet, but I'm working hard on it!
    [*] It's going to be really fun.
[/list]
So what's been going on the last six months of development? I've made a development update video that you can watch [i]right now[/i]! It's here:

[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zs8fn741pww][img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29396689/ac400eae88ecc2d23df3b88fe39c8c35071439bb.png[/img][/url]

For those who don't like videos, here's the gist: I've been down in the slimy guts of the game's internals. It's greasy down there, but sometimes you've got to get your hands dirty.

There is now a proper [b]Saving and Loading System[/b] in the game and this is a Big Deal™ - in-progress zoos can be returned to at a later point! You know, like, in video games.

Because I can easily load previously created zoos, I've been able to work on making sure that the game can be played well with lots of visitors and lots of monsters in it. I'm still working on the performance side of things, but it's coming along!

There's [b]new zoo walls[/b], or rather, fences around the perimeter! They're in the same cast-iron style as the zoo gate, and I think zoos look a lot prettier as a result.

A [b]brand-new camera system![/b] Smooth zooming, rotating, all the good stuff. Good game cameras aren't always the easiest thing to 

[b]Feeding troughs![/b] I like adding new things to the game that the player can actually build, and feeding troughs are a useful addition to monster enclosures. They keep the meat or the cosmic ooze (you know, whatever a monster might be hungry for) organised, because monsters might kick the food out of their pen. These monsters aren't the most intelligent things, but I wouldn't say that near them. I don't know what language they speak, and I don't know if they can read minds or not. What I do know is, [i]they have a lot of teeth.[/i]

I'm excited to have returned from the aforementioned greasy-guts of the game, and back to creating new content. Exciting! If you haven't already, be sure to wishlist the game right here on Steam, and [url=https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCVCz-_8VfkVwgB1WzCcuq4w]subscribe to the youtube channel[/url] (with Bell Button selected and all) to keep up-to-date with exciting development news!

 - Matt
